label: United Pan-African liberation solidarity with Yoruba market women's democracy
description: Active in international Pan-African and anti-imperial networks shaped by W. E. B. Du Bois and Kwame Nkrumah, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti translated Pan-African self-determination into militant Yoruba women's tax resistance.
dialecticalTension: Grounds transnational Pan-African theory in concrete female peasant and market labor.
historicalContext: 1947 Abeokuta Women's Union revolt and 1940s–1950s Pan-African congresses.

citations.author: Cheryl Johnson-Odim & Nina Emma Mba
citations.work: For Women and the Nation: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti of Nigeria

label: Exemplified grassroots African democratic accountability beyond colonial chieftaincy
description: Ransome-Kuti's exposure of how British indirect rule distorted indigenous West African governance into unaccountable autocracy prefigured Kwasi Wiredu's philosophical defense of consensual African democracy.
dialecticalTension: Distinguishes authentic indigenous civic accountability from colonial-invented authoritarianism.
historicalContext: West African political philosophy from anti-colonial mass action to postcolonial critique.

label: Set continent-wide precedent for rural African women's civic-ecological mobilization
description: The Abeokuta Women's Union's mass democratic mobilization led by Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti served as a foundational African precedent for Wangari Maathai's grassroots women's mobilization in Kenya's Green Belt Movement.
dialecticalTension: Links anti-colonial fiscal democracy to postcolonial ecological democracy.

citations.author: Judith Byfield
citations.work: The Bluest Hands: A Social and Economic History of Women Dyers in Abeokuta
